The lead · Relay infrastructure

A Relay Learns to Say No

After repeated outages at nos.lol, its operator reports that a small change inside the relay held back millions of junk read requests.

From the dispatches of someone

The restart was becoming part of the problem. In an account posted Tuesday, the nos.lol operator writing as someone described a relay repeatedly brought down by connection floods and machine chatter. Each restart sent legitimate users rushing back alongside the attackers. The gaps between failures shrank until the service was dying in about a minute.

Firewalls bought time. Around 580 bots were identified and blocked, the operator said, but fresh addresses kept appearing. Shared VPN exits complicated the response: blocking one address could take innocent users with it. Meanwhile, a single spam-filter process became a queue that other workers could not get past.

The reported turning point was roughly fifty lines of request rate limiting inside the relay, applied per address and globally. Excess read requests were refused before reaching its internals. The operator said the relay had rejected over 12 million junk requests and run for 20 hours 50 minutes without a restart at the time of the dispatch.

Requests over the limit are refused before they touch the relay's internals, so the jam has nothing to feed on.

— someone, the operator’s account

The follow-up question reaches beyond attackers. In a later note, someone asked what normal relay use should look like as agents and applications begin treating Nostr as storage, a rendezvous point, or a message bus. The posted threshold was 200 read requests in ten seconds. An open relay still has somebody paying for the door.

The follow-up on client behaviour · Figures are the operator’s reported readings.

Messaging

White Noise Makes Room for the Group

White Noise’s release announcement brings polls to encrypted group chats on iOS and Android, including multiple-choice voting, changeable votes, and an optional closing time. Its larger ambition is ordinary reliability: edits surviving message confirmation, better recovery, and clearer notices when chat history may be missing.

Max said the group ceiling had moved from around 50 members to around 200 and invited users into a larger community chat to test the next limit. He also reported that Android slows considerably beyond 300 groups. Expansion is being accompanied by visible edges, rather than a claim that scale is solved.

White Noise’s release notes · Max’s group test · The Android limit

Release desk

Mostro Retires Its Old Protocol

Mostro Node 0.19.0 removes protocol v1. Its announcement says orders and chat now require a client using protocol v2, with NIP-44. The release also permits makers to cancel before paying a bond and closes disputes on cooperative cancellation or seller release.

Mostro’s announcement

Angor Cleans Up the Plumbing

Angor 0.2.36 reports parallel investment scanning, corrected fee estimation, recovery and founder-claim fixes, and mainnet swaps routed through SatsRouting. Quicker screens sit beside less glamorous fixes to funding and missing UTXOs.

Community tools

The Conversation Wants More Than a Timeline

Reya’s Coop Desktop note put relay groups on the bench. The app catalog offered another route: Team Soapbox describes Armada as community chat with servers, channels, and voice. Cordn presents private group messaging using MLS encryption and Nostr identity.

These are different projects, but the shared direction is clear: give people a room to stay in, alongside the public stream they pass through.

The Instrument

One Shared Note in a Different World

The same 24-hour window, read without this lens, returned 400 notes. Just one also appeared among the 383 ranked notes. Across all fourteen desks, this reading gathered 629 events from 199 voices.

The overlap measures how the selection changes with the reader’s trust lens. It does not certify every claim in the posts. This paper’s window closed at 14:44 UTC on September 30; its pictures, appointments, and reports remain records of that reading.
